title: Audit Procedures for Accounts Receivable
exam_relevance: HEAVILY TESTED - Expect 4-6 questions on CPA AUD exam about A/R confirmation procedures, alternative procedures, allowance testing, and cutoff. This is one of the most tested account-specific procedures.
learning_objectives: Understand confirmation procedures for accounts receivable (primary substantive procedure)
Know the difference between positive and negative confirmations and when to use each
Understand alternative procedures when confirmations are not returned
Know procedures for testing the allowance for doubtful accounts
Understand cutoff testing for accounts receivable
Know how to test aging of accounts receivable
Understand procedures for evaluating collectibility and valuation
Know assertions related to accounts receivable and appropriate procedures for each

introduction.why_important: Accounts receivable is typically a material account in most businesses and is susceptible to overstatement fraud. Confirmation of receivables is considered the most reliable evidence for existence and is generally required by auditing standards.

key_standards.primary: AU-C Section 505 (External Confirmations) - requirements for confirmation procedures
key_standards.related: AU-C Section 330 (Performing Audit Procedures in Response to Assessed Risks)

introduction.exam_importance: A/R confirmations are HEAVILY tested. Know positive vs negative confirmations, alternative procedures, and when confirmation may be omitted.

assertions_for_accounts_receivable.description: Understanding which assertions are at risk helps determine appropriate procedures

existence_occurrence.risk: Recording sales that did not occur or receivables that don't exist (overstatement fraud)
existence_occurrence.primary_procedure: CONFIRMATION - most reliable evidence for existence
other_procedures: Examine subsequent cash receipts (payment after year-end)
Examine sales invoices and shipping documents

completeness.risk: Failing to record valid sales and receivables (understatement)
procedures: Test sales cutoff (ensure sales recorded in correct period)
Trace shipping documents to sales journal
Perform analytical procedures (compare to prior year, industry)
Test for unrecorded sales near year-end

rights_and_obligations.risk: Recording receivables that entity doesn't have rights to collect
procedures: Confirmation (confirms entity's right to receive payment)
Review sales agreements for right of return provisions
Review for pledged or assigned receivables

valuation_accuracy.risk: Receivables recorded at incorrect amounts or not properly valued at net realizable value
procedures: Evaluate credit policies and collection experience
Test mathematical accuracy of A/R subsidiary ledger
Review for proper classification (current vs noncurrent)
Identify related party receivables for separate disclosure
Review for pledged or assigned receivables requiring disclosure
Verify major customer concentrations disclosed if significant

confirmation_procedures.description: External confirmation is the PRIMARY substantive procedure for A/R existence

general_requirement.rule: Auditor is REQUIRED to confirm accounts receivable UNLESS one of three exceptions applies
exceptions_when_confirmation_may_be_omit: 1. A/R is IMMATERIAL to the financial statements
2. Use of confirmations would be INEFFECTIVE (based on prior experience or nature of accounts)
3. Auditor's combined assessed level of INHERENT RISK and CONTROL RISK is LOW, and other substantive procedures provide sufficient evidence
general_requirement.exam_critical: Know the THREE exceptions - frequently tested. Memorize: Immaterial, Ineffective, or low IR+CR with other procedures

timing_of_confirmations.at_year_end: Most reliable - confirms balance as of balance sheet date

before_year_end_interim.allowed: Yes, confirmations can be sent at interim date
before_year_end_interim.requirement: If confirmed at interim, must perform ROLLFORWARD procedures from confirmation date to year-end
rollforward_procedures: Test transactions between confirmation date and year-end
Obtain evidence of subsequent cash receipts
Review significant sales and credits after confirmation date
before_year_end_interim.increased_risk: Fraud or error could occur between confirmation date and year-end

positive_confirmation.definition: Request asks customer to respond whether they AGREE or DISAGREE with stated balance

formats.balance_form: States the customer's balance - asks customer to confirm if correct or provide correct amount
formats.invoice_form: Lists individual invoices - asks customer to confirm
formats.blank_form: DOES NOT state the balance - asks customer to fill in the balance (MOST RELIABLE)

when_to_use: Risk of FRAUD or ERROR is high
positive_confirmation.response_required: Customer must respond in all cases (agreement or disagreement)
positive_confirmation.exam_emphasis: BLANK positive confirmation is MOST RELIABLE because customer must look up balance (can't just sign off)

negative_confirmation.definition: Request asks customer to respond ONLY if they DISAGREE with stated balance
negative_confirmation.assumption: No response = agreement with balance (implicit confirmation)

when_to_use_all_three_conditions_must_be.condition_1: Combined assessed level of INHERENT RISK and CONTROL RISK is LOW
when_to_use_all_three_conditions_must_be.condition_2: Large number of SMALL account balances
when_to_use_all_three_conditions_must_be.condition_3: Auditor has NO REASON to believe recipients will not give adequate consideration to the request

limitations.weaker_evidence: Provides LESS assurance than positive confirmations (no response doesn't guarantee customer agrees)
limitations.unreliable_if_not_returned: Cannot conclude balance is correct just because no response received
limitations.should_not_be_sole_procedure: Generally used in conjunction with other procedures

negative_confirmation.exam_critical: Negative confirmations provide WEAKER evidence. Know the THREE conditions for use.

positive.when_used: Large balances, high risk, disputes, weak controls
positive.blank_form: Most reliable type - customer must determine balance

negative.reliability: Less reliable - no response may mean didn't review
negative.when_used: Low risk + small balances + expect adequate consideration
negative.consideration: Should not be sole substantive procedure

considerations: Include zero balances and credit balances (may indicate unrecorded liabilities)

requirements: Prepared on CLIENT'S letterhead (client is requesting, not auditor)
Addressed to appropriate party who can confirm (accounts payable department)
Return address is AUDITOR'S address (responses come directly to auditor)
step_2_prepare_confirmation_requests.control_requirement: AUDITOR must MAINTAIN CONTROL over confirmation process from preparation through receipt
step_2_prepare_confirmation_requests.exam_critical: Auditor maintains control - prevents client manipulation

step_3_mail_confirmations.requirement: AUDITOR must mail the confirmations (not client)
step_3_mail_confirmations.why: Maintain control and prevent client from intercepting or altering
step_3_mail_confirmations.return_address: Auditor's address so responses come directly to auditor

step_4_follow_up_on_nonresponses.negative_confirmations_not_returned: No follow-up required (no response assumed to be agreement, though weak evidence)
step_4_follow_up_on_nonresponses.second_third_requests: May send second or third confirmation requests before performing alternative procedures

step_5_investigate_exceptions.exception: Customer reports different balance than books
common_causes: Timing differences (payment in mail, goods in transit)
Errors in recording (wrong amount, wrong customer)
step_5_investigate_exceptions.required_action: Investigate ALL exceptions to determine cause and whether adjustment needed

control_over_confirmations.critical_requirement: Auditor must maintain CONTROL over the entire confirmation process
specific_controls: Auditor prepares or supervises preparation of confirmation requests
Responses come directly to AUDITOR (return address is auditor's)
Auditor maintains list of confirmations sent
Auditor directly receives and reviews all responses
control_over_confirmations.why_critical: If client has access to confirmations, they could intercept, alter, or forge responses to conceal fraud
control_over_confirmations.exam_scenario: Question may describe client offering to 'help mail confirmations' - auditor must decline and maintain control

alternative_procedures.when_required: Must perform alternative procedures when POSITIVE confirmations are not returned (after sending second/third requests)
alternative_procedures.not_required_for_negative: Not required for negative confirmations (no response assumed agreement)
alternative_procedures.purpose: Obtain evidence for existence and valuation of receivables by examining subsequent cash receipts and supporting documentation

examine_subsequent_cash_receipts.procedure: Examine subsequent payments received from customer after year-end
examine_subsequent_cash_receipts.evidence_provided: Payment provides strong evidence that receivable existed and was valid
how_to_perform: Trace specific invoices making up year-end balance to subsequent cash receipts
Examine bank deposit slips showing receipt
Examine customer remittance advices showing which invoices were paid
examine_subsequent_cash_receipts.exam_emphasis: Subsequent cash receipts is PRIMARY alternative procedure - strongly supports existence

examine_shipping_documents.procedure: Examine shipping documents (bills of lading, delivery receipts) supporting the sale
examine_shipping_documents.evidence_provided: Shows goods were shipped to customer
documents_to_examine: Shipping documents (bill of lading, delivery receipts)
examine_shipping_documents.limitation: Shows shipment occurred but doesn't prove customer accepted or will pay

examine_sales_invoices_and_orders.procedure: Examine sales invoices and customer purchase orders
examine_sales_invoices_and_orders.evidence_provided: Shows terms of sale and customer's order
examine_sales_invoices_and_orders.limitation: Internal documents are weaker than external evidence

sufficiency_of_alternative_procedures.combination_required: Typically need COMBINATION of alternative procedures (subsequent receipts + shipping documents)
sufficiency_of_alternative_procedures.subsequent_receipts_strongest: Examining subsequent cash receipts is most persuasive alternative procedure
sufficiency_of_alternative_procedures.if_no_subsequent_payment: If customer hasn't paid after year-end, must rely more heavily on shipping documentation and may need to assess collectibility

exam_question_pattern.scenario: Customer did not return positive confirmation. What should auditor do?
wrong_answers: Accept the nonresponse as confirmation (NO - only for negative confirmations)
Assume balance is in error (NO - just means need alternative procedures)
exam_question_pattern.correct_answer: Perform alternative procedures: examine subsequent cash receipts and shipping documentation

testing_allowance_for_doubtful_accounts.description: Allowance for doubtful accounts is a significant estimate - auditor must evaluate reasonableness
testing_allowance_for_doubtful_accounts.why_important: Management can manipulate earnings by over/understating the allowance. This is a fraud risk area.

understanding_the_allowance.purpose: Reduce gross A/R to net realizable value (amount expected to be collected)
understanding_the_allowance.accounting: Contra-asset account that reduces A/R on balance sheet
understanding_the_allowance.fraud_risk: Can be manipulated to manage earnings (understate allowance = overstate income)

review_aging_of_receivables.procedure: Obtain and test accounts receivable aging schedule
steps: Obtain client-prepared aging (categorizes receivables by days outstanding: current, 30-60, 60-90, over 90)
Test accuracy: trace sample of individual receivables to aging to verify correct classification
Reconcile aging total to general ledger A/R balance
review_aging_of_receivables.why_important: Aging is basis for determining allowance - must be accurate
review_aging_of_receivables.red_flag: Large amounts in old categories (over 90 days) suggest collection problems

analyze_historical_collection_rates.procedure: Analyze historical bad debt write-offs and collection experience
steps: Calculate historical bad debt percentage (write-offs / credit sales) for prior years
Compare current allowance percentage to historical rates
Evaluate whether historical rates are reasonable basis for current estimate
analyze_historical_collection_rates.expectation: Current allowance % should be consistent with historical experience unless conditions changed
analyze_historical_collection_rates.exam_tip: If allowance is significantly lower than historical rates, may be understated (red flag)

examine_subsequent_collections.procedure: Examine subsequent cash collections after year-end
examine_subsequent_collections.logic: Accounts that are paid after year-end were collectible - didn't need to be in allowance. Accounts NOT paid may need to be written off.
steps: For aged receivables (especially over 90 days), check if subsequently collected
If not collected after reasonable time, evaluate whether should be written off
Calculate what % of year-end receivables were ultimately uncollectible
examine_subsequent_collections.strong_evidence: Subsequent collections provide objective evidence of collectibility

review_credit_policies_and_collection_pr.procedure: Understand and evaluate client's credit policies and collection efforts
considerations: Have credit policies changed (loosened or tightened)?
Is company aggressively collecting or being lenient?
Are there specific customers in financial difficulty?
Has customer base changed (new customers vs established customers)?
review_credit_policies_and_collection_pr.impact: Changes in credit policy or customer financial health may require higher/lower allowance

develop_independent_estimate.procedure: Auditor develops own expectation of reasonable allowance

aging_method.calculation: Apply different percentages to each aging category based on historical collection rates

develop_independent_estimate.comparison: Compare auditor's estimate to management's allowance
develop_independent_estimate.if_difference_material: Discuss with management, obtain explanation, consider adjustment

evaluate_specific_accounts.procedure: Review specific large or unusual receivables for collectibility
focus_on: Customers known to be in financial difficulty
evaluate_specific_accounts.specific_reserve: May need specific reserves for known uncollectible accounts in addition to general allowance

review_management_representations.requirement: Obtain written representation from management about allowance adequacy
review_management_representations.representation: Management represents that allowance is adequate to reduce receivables to net realizable value

red_flags_inadequate_allowance: Allowance % decreased from prior year with no explanation
Allowance % lower than historical collection experience
Significant aged receivables (over 90 days) with low allowance
Deteriorating customer financial condition not reflected in allowance
Management facing pressure to meet earnings targets (incentive to understate allowance)
Significant accounts not collected after year-end but not reserved
testing_allowance_for_doubtful_accounts.exam_emphasis: Know how to evaluate allowance reasonableness: historical rates, aging analysis, subsequent collections. Understand that understated allowance = overstated income = fraud risk.

cutoff_testing.description: Cutoff testing ensures sales are recorded in the correct accounting period (completeness and occurrence)

purpose.sales_occurrence: Ensure sales recorded in current period actually occurred before year-end (no premature revenue recognition)
purpose.sales_completeness: Ensure sales that occurred before year-end were recorded (not deferred to next period)

cutoff_concern_both_directions.overstatement_risk: Recording sales in current year that belong in next year (inflate current year revenue)
cutoff_concern_both_directions.understatement_risk: Failing to record sales that occurred before year-end (understated revenue)
cutoff_concern_both_directions.exam_note: Cutoff tests BOTH directions - before and after year-end

examine_sales_near_year_end.procedure: Select sales transactions recorded shortly before and after year-end

for_sales_recorded_before_year_end.examine: Shipping documents (bills of lading, delivery receipts)
for_sales_recorded_before_year_end.verify: Goods were actually shipped BEFORE year-end date
for_sales_recorded_before_year_end.red_flag: Sale recorded Dec 31 but shipped Jan 3 = improper cutoff (should be next period)

for_sales_recorded_after_year_end.verify: Goods were shipped AFTER year-end (not before)
for_sales_recorded_after_year_end.red_flag: Sale recorded Jan 2 but shipped Dec 29 = improper cutoff (should be current period)

fob_shipping_point.rule: Sale recorded when goods SHIP (title passes when shipped)

fob_destination.rule: Sale recorded when goods ARRIVE at customer (title passes on delivery)

shipping_terms_matter.exam_critical: Must consider shipping terms when evaluating cutoff

review_sales_journal.procedure: Review sales journal for unusual patterns near year-end
red_flags: Spike in sales in last few days of year (channel stuffing)
Large credits or returns shortly after year-end (suggests premature recognition)
Sales to unusual customers near year-end

examine_bill_and_hold_transactions.definition: Customer purchases goods but goods remain at seller's location
examine_bill_and_hold_transactions.risk: Seller may record sale before revenue recognition criteria met
revenue_recognition_criteria: Reason for bill-and-hold arrangement is substantive
Product is separately identified as belonging to customer
Seller cannot use product or direct it to another customer
examine_bill_and_hold_transactions.audit_procedure: Review bill-and-hold transactions near year-end for proper revenue recognition

cash_receipts_cutoff.procedure: Test cutoff of cash receipts to ensure applied to receivables in correct period
cash_receipts_cutoff.examine: Cash receipts journal before and after year-end
cash_receipts_cutoff.verify: Cash received before year-end reduced receivables in current year (not next year)
cash_receipts_cutoff.timing_issue: Check dated before year-end but deposited after year-end - typically record when received

cutoff_testing.exam_tip: Cutoff questions: Look at SHIPPING DATE (or delivery date for FOB destination). Sale should be recorded when title passes based on shipping terms.

analytical_procedures.description: Analytical procedures provide overall reasonableness test for A/R and identify unusual relationships

receivables_turnover_ratio.calculation: Net credit sales ÷ Average accounts receivable
receivables_turnover_ratio.interpretation: Higher ratio = faster collection. Lower than expected may indicate collection problems or overstated receivables.
receivables_turnover_ratio.comparison: Compare to prior years and industry averages

days_sales_in_receivables.calculation: 365 ÷ Receivables turnover ratio OR (A/R ÷ Credit sales) × 365
days_sales_in_receivables.interpretation: Number of days sales in receivables. Higher than expected may indicate collection problems or slow-moving receivables.
days_sales_in_receivables.example: If 60 days but company has 30-day terms, suggests collection issues

allowance_as_percentage_of_ar.calculation: Allowance for doubtful accounts ÷ Gross A/R
allowance_as_percentage_of_ar.interpretation: Should be relatively stable unless credit policies or customer base changes
allowance_as_percentage_of_ar.comparison: Compare to prior years - significant decrease may indicate understated allowance

ar_as_percentage_of_current_assets.interpretation: Should be relatively stable. Significant changes may indicate issues
ar_as_percentage_of_current_assets.comparison: Compare to prior years and industry

comparison_of_ar_to_sales.procedure: Compare monthly A/R balances to monthly sales
comparison_of_ar_to_sales.expectation: Should move together - if sales increase, A/R should increase proportionally
comparison_of_ar_to_sales.red_flag: Sales increase but A/R doesn't increase = collection problems OR premature revenue recognition

when_performed.planning: Analytical procedures in planning identify risk areas
when_performed.substantive: Substantive analytical procedures provide evidence about account balance
when_performed.final_review: Analytical procedures in final review ensure reasonableness

test_mathematical_accuracy.procedure: Test mathematical accuracy of A/R subsidiary ledger
steps: Reconcile subsidiary ledger total to general ledger control account

review_for_related_party_receivables.procedure: Identify any receivables from related parties
review_for_related_party_receivables.requirement: Related party receivables must be separately disclosed
review_for_related_party_receivables.concern: Related party transactions may not be at arm's length

review_for_pledged_assigned_receivables.procedure: Review loan agreements and board minutes for pledging or assignment of receivables
examples: Receivables pledged as collateral for loan
Receivables sold (factored) with or without recourse
review_for_pledged_assigned_receivables.disclosure: Must be disclosed in financial statements
review_for_pledged_assigned_receivables.assertion: Rights and obligations, presentation and disclosure

test_for_credit_balances.procedure: Review A/R for credit balances (customer overpayments)
test_for_credit_balances.reclassification: Credit balances should be reclassified to accounts payable (current liability)
test_for_credit_balances.why: Credit balance means company owes customer - it's a liability, not an asset

problem_1.question:
An auditor is planning the accounts receivable confirmation procedures. Which of the following situations would be MOST appropriate for using negative confirmations?

A) The combined assessed level of inherent and control risk is high, accounts consist of many small balances, and the auditor believes customers will give adequate consideration to the requests.

B) The combined assessed level of inherent and control risk is low, accounts consist of many small balances, and the auditor believes customers will give adequate consideration to the requests.

C) The combined assessed level of inherent and control risk is low, accounts consist of a few large balances, and the auditor believes customers will give adequate consideration to the requests.

D) Individual account balances are large and there is evidence of disputes with several customers.
problem_1.explanation:
Negative confirmations can ONLY be used when ALL THREE conditions are met: (1) combined assessed level of inherent risk and control risk is LOW, (2) large number of SMALL account balances, and (3) auditor has no reason to believe recipients will not give adequate consideration. Only option B meets all three conditions.

A is wrong - high risk requires positive confirmations.
C is wrong - large balances require positive confirmations.
D is wrong - disputes require positive confirmations.
problem_1.exam_tip: Remember the THREE conditions for negative confirmations (must have ALL three): Low IR+CR, Small balances, Adequate consideration expected. If any condition not met, must use positive confirmations.

problem_2.question:
An auditor sent positive confirmations for year-end accounts receivable. Several confirmations were not returned despite sending second and third requests. Which of the following would be the MOST appropriate alternative procedure?

A) Send negative confirmations to the non-responding customers.

B) Review the aged trial balance for significant past-due accounts.

C) Examine subsequent cash receipts and sales invoices for the non-responding accounts.

D) Increase the allowance for doubtful accounts.
problem_2.explanation:
When positive confirmations are not returned, the auditor must perform ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURES. The most appropriate alternative procedure is to examine SUBSEQUENT CASH RECEIPTS (shows receivable existed and was collectible) and supporting documentation (sales invoices, shipping documents).

A is wrong - cannot switch from positive to negative confirmations for nonresponses.
B is wrong - reviewing aged trial balance is helpful but doesn't provide specific evidence for the individual accounts.
D is wrong - no basis to increase allowance just because confirmation not returned - need to investigate first.
problem_2.exam_tip: PRIMARY alternative procedure for nonresponses: Examine subsequent cash receipts (strong evidence for existence and collectibility) and shipping documentation.

problem_3.question:
An auditor is testing the allowance for doubtful accounts. Which of the following procedures would provide the BEST evidence regarding the reasonableness of the allowance?

A) Confirming accounts receivable with customers.

B) Examining subsequent cash collections and comparing historical bad debt percentages to the current allowance.

C) Reviewing the aging schedule for mathematical accuracy.

D) Obtaining management's representation that the allowance is adequate.
problem_3.explanation:
The BEST evidence for evaluating the allowance is examining SUBSEQUENT CASH COLLECTIONS (shows which receivables were collectible vs. which should have been reserved) and comparing HISTORICAL BAD DEBT RATES to the current allowance percentage (indicates whether current allowance is consistent with experience).

A is wrong - confirmations test existence, not valuation/allowance adequacy.
C is wrong - testing mathematical accuracy is important but doesn't evaluate whether the allowance AMOUNT is reasonable.
D is wrong - management representation is required but is the weakest form of evidence (self-serving).
problem_3.exam_tip: Allowance testing: (1) Historical bad debt rates, (2) Subsequent collections, (3) Aging analysis. Subsequent collections = objective evidence of collectibility.

problem_4.question:
Which of the following is a valid reason for an auditor to OMIT confirmation of accounts receivable?

A) The client requests that confirmations not be sent because it might upset customers.

B) Accounts receivable is immaterial to the financial statements.

C) The auditor believes the confirmation process would be too time-consuming.

D) The client has never had problems with accounts receivable in the past.
problem_4.explanation:
Confirmation of A/R is REQUIRED unless one of THREE exceptions applies: (1) A/R is IMMATERIAL, (2) confirmations would be INEFFECTIVE, or (3) combined assessed IR and CR is LOW and other substantive procedures provide sufficient evidence. Option B (immaterial) is a valid exception.

A is wrong - client preference is NOT a valid reason to omit confirmations.
C is wrong - time/cost is not a valid reason to omit required procedures.
D is wrong - past experience alone doesn't justify omitting confirmations unless meets one of the three exceptions.
problem_4.exam_tip: THREE exceptions to A/R confirmation requirement: (1) Immaterial, (2) Ineffective, (3) Low IR+CR with other procedures. Client preference is NEVER a valid reason.

problem_5.question:
An auditor is testing sales cutoff at year-end (December 31). The auditor selects a sales transaction recorded on December 30 for $50,000. The shipping document shows the goods were shipped FOB shipping point on January 2. What should the auditor conclude?

A) The sale is properly recorded because it was invoiced before year-end.

B) The sale should be reversed and recorded in the next period because goods shipped after year-end.

C) The sale is acceptable if the customer ordered the goods before year-end.

D) No adjustment needed if the customer paid for the goods before year-end.
problem_5.explanation:
For FOB SHIPPING POINT sales, revenue should be recognized when goods are SHIPPED (title passes at shipping point). Since the goods were shipped AFTER year-end (January 2), the sale recorded on December 30 is IMPROPER CUTOFF. The sale should be reversed from current period and recorded in next period.

A is wrong - invoice date is not determinative; shipping date determines revenue recognition for FOB shipping point.
C is wrong - customer order date doesn't determine revenue recognition.
D is wrong - payment timing doesn't determine revenue recognition.
problem_5.exam_tip: Cutoff testing: For FOB shipping point, use SHIPPING DATE. For FOB destination, use DELIVERY DATE. Sale should match shipping terms.

tip_1_confirmation_is_required.rule: Confirmation of A/R is REQUIRED unless one of three exceptions
tip_1_confirmation_is_required.three_exceptions: 1) Immaterial, 2) Ineffective, 3) Low IR+CR with other procedures
tip_1_confirmation_is_required.exam_question: Why can auditor omit confirmations? Must be one of three exceptions
tip_1_confirmation_is_required.wrong_answer: Client preference, cost, time - NOT valid reasons

positive_confirmations.when: Large balances, high risk, disputes, weak controls
positive_confirmations.response: Must respond whether agree or disagree

negative_confirmations.when: ALL three conditions: Low IR+CR + Small balances + Adequate consideration
negative_confirmations.exam_trap: Don't pick negative if any condition not met

tip_3_alternative_procedures.best_procedure: Examine SUBSEQUENT CASH RECEIPTS (strongest alternative evidence)
tip_3_alternative_procedures.also: Examine shipping documents and sales invoices
tip_3_alternative_procedures.exam_question: What to do when confirmation not returned? Perform alternative procedures

tip_4_auditor_maintains_control.critical: Auditor must CONTROL entire confirmation process
specifically: Responses come to AUDITOR'S address (not client)
tip_4_auditor_maintains_control.why: Prevent client from intercepting, altering, or forging responses
tip_4_auditor_maintains_control.exam_scenario: Client offers to mail - auditor must decline

key_procedures: Historical bad debt rates (compare to current allowance %)
Aging analysis (test accuracy, evaluate old accounts)
tip_5_allowance_testing.red_flag: Allowance decreased from prior year or lower than historical rates = possible understatement
tip_5_allowance_testing.fraud_risk: Management may understate allowance to inflate income
tip_5_allowance_testing.exam_emphasis: Know how to evaluate allowance reasonableness

tip_6_cutoff_testing.tests_both_directions: Before year-end (not premature) AND after year-end (not omitted)
tip_6_cutoff_testing.key_document: SHIPPING DOCUMENTS (bills of lading, delivery receipts)
tip_6_cutoff_testing.exam_question: Look at shipping date and compare to sale date. Should match based on shipping terms.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: When can auditor omit A/R confirmations?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Must be one of three exceptions: Immaterial, Ineffective, or Low IR+CR with other procedures

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Positive vs negative confirmations - which to use?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Negative only if ALL three conditions (Low IR+CR, Small balances, Adequate consideration). Otherwise positive.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Confirmation not returned - what to do?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: If POSITIVE: perform alternative procedures (subsequent receipts + shipping docs). If NEGATIVE: no follow-up needed.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: How to test allowance for doubtful accounts?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Historical rates, subsequent collections, aging analysis, develop independent estimate
Compare shipping date to sale date. Consider shipping terms (FOB shipping point vs destination).
AUDITOR must mail and maintain control (not client)

memorization_aids.three_exceptions_to_confirmations: IME: Immaterial, iMeffective (ineffective), low risk with Evidence
memorization_aids.three_conditions_for_negative: LSA: Low risk, Small balances, Adequate consideration
memorization_aids.alternative_procedures: CASH is king - Subsequent CASH receipts is primary alternative procedure
memorization_aids.cutoff: Ship it - FOB Shipping point = recognize when SHIPPED

key_concepts: Confirmation of A/R is PRIMARY substantive procedure for existence (required unless exception)
Three exceptions to confirmation: Immaterial, Ineffective, or Low IR+CR with other procedures
Positive confirmations: more reliable, required for large balances/high risk, nonresponse requires alternative procedures
Negative confirmations: weaker evidence, only when Low IR+CR + Small balances + Adequate consideration
Blank positive confirmation is MOST reliable (customer must determine balance)
Auditor must MAINTAIN CONTROL over confirmation process (prepare, mail, receive responses)
Alternative procedures for nonresponses: examine subsequent cash receipts (primary) and shipping documents
Allowance testing: historical rates, subsequent collections, aging analysis, develop independent estimate
Cutoff testing: verify sales recorded in correct period based on shipping date and terms
Analytical procedures: receivables turnover, days sales in receivables, allowance as % of A/R
critical_for_exam: Know THREE exceptions to A/R confirmation requirement
Know THREE conditions for using negative confirmations (must have ALL three)
Auditor maintains control over confirmations (mails them, receives responses)
Alternative procedures for nonresponses: subsequent cash receipts + shipping docs
Blank positive confirmation is MOST reliable type
Allowance testing: historical rates and subsequent collections are key
Cutoff: use shipping date for FOB shipping point
common_mistakes: Thinking client preference is valid reason to omit confirmations (NO - must be one of three exceptions)
Using negative confirmations when high risk or large balances (NO - need all three conditions)
Thinking no response to negative confirmation means balance is confirmed (weak evidence)
Not recognizing need for alternative procedures when positive confirmations not returned
